subject.title: bug: Duplicate messages sent to Slack

question: Can a maintainer or operator correlate the named Slack session to gateway delivery logs and Slack message IDs well enough to identify which duplicate-delivery class occurred?
rationale: The private session/log evidence is the difference between an implemented-on-main close and a new code fix; source inspection alone leaves multiple plausible roots open.

options.title: Keep for log correlation
options.body: Inspect the named session, gateway delivery queue state, and the two Slack message IDs before deciding whether current main already fixed the class.

options.title: Close as implemented after matching logs
options.body: Close only if the logs match a specific current-main or shipped fix such as Slack preview fallback, turn-local duplicate suppression, or durable unknown-send reconciliation.

options.title: Scope a focused fix
options.body: If logs show a remaining duplicate path, file or land one targeted regression in the Slack delivery or outbound queue path instead of adding broad speculative dedupe.

recommendation.title: Keep for log correlation
recommendation.body: Inspect the named session, gateway delivery queue state, and the two Slack message IDs before deciding whether current main already fixed the class.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing candidate from the nearby Slack duplicate-delivery and inbound dedupe fix history.
